topic: Water-quality stations along the working river
visual: A sparse point portrait of monitoring locations along a bounded Ohio River reach around Cincinnati.
data: Water Quality Portal station metadata, filtered to a stated river reach and retrieval window.
fallback: One verified public monitoring network instead of a cross-provider query.
caveat: A station's presence does not establish recent sampling or complete analyte coverage.

topic: Night survey: an unlabeled contour portrait
visual: Approved 24 km crop B around Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky; pale contours on dark blue-green; viewers guess the location.
data: Already cached USGS 3DEP one-third arc-second tiles n40w085 and n39w085.
fallback: Retain the verified native-R composition; make only reviewed editorial adjustments.
caveat: No separate water mask; roughly 10 m source spacing is not vertical accuracy. The native-R pipeline and executing draft post are verified, but not published.

visual: HUC12 catchments around Cincinnati, showing that drainage boundaries ignore the Ohio/Kentucky administrative split.
data: USGS Watershed Boundary Dataset catchments intersecting a deliberately bounded regional extent.
fallback: Use a smaller set of HUC10 catchments if the HUC12 view is too busy.
caveat: Watersheds were previously suggested, not approved. Confirm scale and scope before implementation.

visual: Observed street-tree clusters using a restrained point-density or DBSCAN treatment, rather than a rainbow heatmap.
data: Candidate municipal public tree inventory; if unavailable, explicitly labeled OSM mapped-tree observations.
fallback: A hex-binned count of observed records in one neighborhood.
caveat: Verify inventory availability, license and coverage first. Recording density is not necessarily true tree density; justify clustering parameters.

topic: What the river overlooks can see
visual: Terrain horizons or a small set of line-of-sight transects from public overlooks above the Ohio.
data: USGS 3DEP terrain and verified public overlook coordinates.
fallback: One annotated cross-river elevation transect rather than a full viewshed.
caveat: A bare-earth horizon omits buildings and trees. State observer height and do not claim photographic visibility.

topic: The riverfront through an old topographic sheet
visual: A tightly cropped historical USGS topographic map with one carefully chosen modern reference layer.
data: Candidate georeferenced historical Cincinnati topographic sheet from USGS topoView.
fallback: A clearly labeled present-day map using an archival engraving treatment, not a fake historical reconstruction.
caveat: Record the actual sheet edition and survey dates; check georeferencing and rights. Never imply current features existed on the historic survey.

visual: Build a deliberately simple river-access map inside the theme's ten-minute construction limit.
data: Previously cached river geometry and verified public access points.
fallback: One river reach, one line and a small set of labeled access points.
caveat: Time the actual map-making block and disclose pre-cached inputs; do not pretend data preparation fit the same ten minutes.

topic: A city where every neighborhood reaches a park
visual: Compare an explicit idealized park-access scenario with existing pedestrian access, using a small bounded area.
data: Candidate public park boundaries and cached OSM pedestrian network.
fallback: Clearly labeled straight-line park buffers with no walking-time claim.
caveat: Utopia is a scenario, not a forecast. State network restrictions, assumed travel speed and missing entrances.

visual: An impervious-cover gradient from Cincinnati's urban core into its rural surroundings.
data: A stated edition of USGS Annual NLCD land-cover or impervious-surface data.
fallback: One urban-to-rural transect with transparent land-cover classes.
caveat: Urban and rural labels depend on definition; distinguish mapped land cover from population or administrative categories.

topic: One map, built through prompts only
visual: A controlled prompt-only exercise that generates a native-R map from an already verified cached dataset.
data: Reuse the Day01 station cache or another approved small public dataset, with data access constrained to the cache.
packages: R packages chosen by the bounded prompt, executed as native R
fallback: A minimal two-layer sf map from the same cache.
caveat: Confirm what the official prompt-only constraint means for code edits. Keep prompts, generated R, errors and corrections; no fabricated coordinates or unverifiable data.

visual: Map distance from major transport corridors as a clearly labeled noise-exposure proxy.
data: Cached OSM major-road, rail and airport geometries over a small Cincinnati extent.
fallback: Distance to major roads only, without combining incomparable source types.
caveat: These are proximity indicators, not measured decibels or a validated acoustic model. Record OSM incompleteness and source-date limitations.

visual: Map electricity-generating plants along a bounded river corridor, with capacity and fuel represented separately.
data: Candidate EIA-860 public plant coordinates, fuel and nameplate-capacity fields for a stated year.
fallback: One plant type or one state segment of the corridor.
caveat: Nameplate capacity is not generation, availability or river impact. Validate coordinate quality and plant status.

visual: Confluences, contributing catchments and surrounding developed land in a small set of tributary mouths.
data: USGS hydrography plus a compatible land-cover edition.
fallback: A purely geometric confluence map without land-cover statistics.
caveat: Distinguish spatial coincidence from causal evidence about water quality or urban effects.

topic: A river inside a map inside a river
visual: Nested maps move from one river bend to the metropolitan reach and then its drainage basin, making the map's own scale structure visible.
data: One consistent public hydrography source and verified nested extents.
fallback: Three finite nested panels with explicit extent connectors.
caveat: Treat the Borgesian theme as a deliberate scale/representation experiment, not a claim to an infinite or literal 1:1 map.

visual: Invert the usual figure-ground relationship: water becomes the solid subject and land becomes the surrounding void.
data: Verified Ohio River water polygons clipped to the chosen Cincinnati extent.
fallback: A single reliable river polygon with simple clipping.
caveat: Check holes, islands, polygon validity and shoreline date. This is cartographic inversion, not a change in hydrology.

topic: A shared map of places worth keeping
visual: A small, consent-based collection of public places supplied by real collaborators, with contributor-approved short captions.
data: Actual volunteered locations and captions, recorded with permission and source provenance.
source: Human contributions collected for this issue; no submissions exist yet.
fallback: A two-person collaboration with a small number of verified public locations.
caveat: Requires real participation; do not synthesize contributors or captions. Do not expose homes, routines or private coordinates.

visual: Paired terrain-relief maps show how illumination direction changes the apparent reading of Cincinnati's hills.
data: Reuse the verified raw USGS DEM cache, rebuilding the derived surfaces in R.
fallback: One hillshade with two explicitly stated illumination settings in adjacent panels.
caveat: Modeled illumination is not observed daylight or a prediction of building shadows. Keep terrain, scale and contrast fixed for comparison.

visual: Make missing monitoring information visible without translating missing values into zero concentration.
data: A narrowly scoped Water Quality Portal query with station/analyte/time coverage recorded explicitly.
fallback: A map of which queried stations have usable records versus returned-but-unusable records.
caveat: The official theme is the literal string NULL. No returned record means no record in this query, not proof of no monitoring or no contamination.

topic: A speculative scent map of the city
visual: Observed coffee roasters, bakeries and breweries become a restrained map of plausible smell sources.
data: Candidate verified public business locations, beginning with OSM tags and manual public-source checks.
fallback: One source category with a small verified set of locations.
caveat: Locations are odor-source proxies, not a measured smell plume. No exposure, nuisance or health claim; do not invent wind modeling.

visual: Equal-area hexagons summarize verified monitoring-location counts along the regional river corridor.
data: Reuse a scoped station cache with duplicate stations resolved explicitly.
fallback: One fixed hex size and count per cell, with a transparent zero/missing distinction.
caveat: Justify cell size and equal-area CRS. Counts are records or distinct locations as stated, not sampling effort or coverage quality.

visual: An OpenStreetMap-only map of mapped pedestrian river crossings and their approach connections.
data: Cached OSM bridges, paths and access tags around Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky.
fallback: A verified static bridge-and-approach geometry map without routing.
caveat: Credit OpenStreetMap contributors and honor ODbL. Mapped access can be incomplete or outdated; do not present routes as current safety guidance.

visual: Show the Ohio basin in a suitable equal-area projection beside Web Mercator, with measured area distortion and honest scale framing.
data: One public basin outline reused unchanged between projections.
fallback: Compare equal-area and conformal projections over a broader extent if local distortion is visually negligible.
caveat: A city-scale projection comparison may be imperceptible. Explain which property is preserved and calculate distortion from real geometry, not illustration tricks.

visual: A small verified set of public chili-restaurant locations, showing geography rather than rankings.
data: Candidate OSM restaurant records checked against current public business information.
fallback: A clearly bounded sample with explicit inclusion rules.
caveat: Do not claim completeness, quality, popularity or cultural representativeness from a convenience sample. No review-site scraping is assumed.

visual: A small pedestrian/cycle bridge network highlights how removing one crossing changes connectivity in the modeled graph.
data: Cached OSM network with verified access tags and a deliberately limited extent.
fallback: A connectivity diagram of verified crossings without travel-time claims.
caveat: This is a graph scenario, not a live closure report. Validate topology, direction, modes and restrictions; do not equate model disconnection with real-world isolation.

topic: A score for the river valley
visual: Stack real cross-river elevation transects into a map-like score that withholds a conventional basemap.
data: Actual transects sampled from the USGS DEM, with orientation and spacing preserved in the method.
packages: terra, sf, base R graphics or grid
fallback: A small number of clearly located profiles with a tiny key after the reveal.
caveat: State which spatial relationships survive the transformation; artistic layout must not masquerade as an ordinary plan-view map.

topic: A river measured in moving water
visual: Map stream gauges along a bounded Ohio River reach using discharge from a common, stated observation window.
data: Candidate USGS public gauge locations and discharge observations, with units and observation times checked.
packages: sf, dplyr, mapsf; native R HTTP acquisition
fallback: Gauge locations plus a short, explicitly asynchronous observation table if comparable discharge is unavailable.
caveat: Check API availability, provisional flags, units and timestamps. No interpolation between gauges or flood-risk inference without a defensible method.

topic: A new cartographic grammar for the same city
visual: Use a genuinely new-to-this-campaign R mapping package for a small public park-area or neighborhood context map.
data: Candidate municipal public neighborhood and park boundaries with explicit area denominator.
packages: mapsf or tmap static mode, whichever is genuinely new by this day
fallback: A simpler static map in the chosen new package, not a return to the familiar renderer.
caveat: Confirm the package is actually new relative to prior completed days, validate dependencies, and avoid treating package novelty as a substitute for a clear question.

visual: A small set of public walking segments colored by terrain grade as an invitation to discuss how the city feels on foot.
data: OSM public paths plus USGS elevation sampled consistently along each segment.
fallback: One public hill walk with an elevation profile and no modeled travel-time score.
caveat: Slope is a physical proxy, not a universal measure of effort, accessibility or emotion. Do not expose private habitual routes; describe limitations.

visual: A deliberately raster-first distance field makes the river's spatial reach visible without using administrative polygons.
data: Verified river-water geometry rasterized on an explicitly projected grid; distance derived in R.
fallback: A coarse Euclidean distance raster over the same bounded extent.
caveat: Euclidean distance is not walking access, hydrologic connectivity, groundwater influence or flood risk. Record cell size and units.

visual: An R-generated printable river/contour sheet invites a real hand-drawn annotation, with the final artifact documented in the post.
data: Reuse verified public terrain or hydrography and, if approved, an actual contributed paper sketch.
packages: sf, terra, base R graphics; R-only image handling if a scan is used
fallback: An explicitly labeled R-generated pen-style field sheet if Sean prefers no physical-paper step.
caveat: Confirm how to reconcile the literal Pen & paper theme with the all-R implementation rule. Do not silently grant an exception or invent a hand-drawn contribution.
